I will keep to the cropping pattern I know best: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. In Quzhou, that is the steadiest way for me to use the year, and at my age I would rather stay with crops I understand well, can sell easily, and can manage without taking big risks. I will not spread myself across many crops. Wheat gives me a secure main crop through spring and early summer, and maize fits right after harvest with the local heat and rain. I will use improved or hybrid seed, but I will keep management moderate instead of chasing the highest possible yield. I will put enough fertilizer to keep the crop steady, irrigate when the crop truly needs it, and spray only when pest or disease pressure is real. For wheat, I will focus on basal fertilizer, one topdressing, a few irrigations at key stages, and basic control of aphids, rust, and weeds. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize, mostly with no-tillage or very light tillage so I save labor and catch soil moisture. For maize, I will keep plant stand even, add nitrogen in stages, irrigate if the summer rain is short, and control weeds and borers with limited sprays. This is the plan I would trust for a stable year.
